tour.overview:
Before oil and gas, Qatar lived from the sea: from pearl diving, fishing and trade with the ports of the Gulf. The north of the peninsula is where that world can still be seen. This private day trip leaves Doha's towers behind and follows the coast to the places that tell the story of old Qatar, with a local guide and a private car.

The highlight is Al Zubarah, on the north-west coast. In the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries it was one of the great pearl-trading towns of the Gulf, a walled port with markets, houses and palaces. Abandoned in the early twentieth century and covered by sand, the town is now an archaeological site listed by UNESCO in 2013, and its square fort, built in 1938, houses a small exhibition. Nearby lies Al Jumail, a fishing village abandoned when its people moved to the cities, where coral-stone houses and a mosque stand in silence by the sea.

The second half of the day turns east to the mangroves of Al Thakhira, the largest in Qatar, where you can paddle a kayak through the channels at high tide or walk along the shore to watch herons and flamingos. The trip ends at Purple Island, named after a dye that ancient settlers made from sea snails, and the harbour of Al Khor, once a pearling port, before the drive back to Doha.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 8 hours
• Start and finish: your hotel in Doha
• Distance: about 300 km round trip
• Type: private tour with car, driver and English-speaking local guide
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Activity level: easy; the kayak is optional

WHAT YOU SEE
• Al Zubarah Archaeological Site and Al Zubarah Fort.
• The abandoned village of Al Jumail.
• The Al Thakhira mangroves.
• Purple Island (Jazirat Bin Ghanim).
• Al Khor harbour and corniche.

WHY THIS TOUR WORKS
The sites of North Qatar are far apart and have little signage, so a guide makes the difference between ruins and a story. Doing them in a single private day lets you time the mangroves for the tide and Al Zubarah for the softer light.

WHO WILL ENJOY IT
Travellers interested in history and heritage, nature and bird lovers, photographers, and visitors who have already seen Doha.

WHO MIGHT PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you only have half a day, our Doha city tour or our West Qatar tour are shorter. For dunes and adventure, choose the desert safari to the Inland Sea.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Wear comfortable shoes, a hat and sunscreen, and bring swimwear or a change of clothes if you plan to kayak. Insect repellent helps in the mangroves in the evening. Lunch is taken in Al Khor or on the way and is not included.

days.name: North Qatar Day Trip
days.description:
What to expect: a full private day in the north of Qatar – the UNESCO site and fort of Al Zubarah, the abandoned village of Al Jumail, the mangroves of Al Thakhira, Purple Island and Al Khor.

Your guide and driver collect you from your hotel in the morning. The road runs north-west across the flat interior of the peninsula, past farms and low limestone ridges, to Al Zubarah, about an hour and a half from Doha. In the eighteenth century this was one of the richest pearling and trading towns in the Gulf, with a town wall, a harbour, markets and courtyard houses. The town was abandoned in the early twentieth century and slowly buried by sand; excavations have uncovered its streets, and in 2013 it became Qatar's first UNESCO World Heritage Site. Your guide explains how the pearl trade worked as you walk to a viewpoint over the excavated town, then you visit Al Zubarah Fort, a square fort with round and rectangular towers built in 1938 to guard the coast, which now holds an exhibition on the site.

A short drive north brings you to Al Jumail, a fishing village of coral-stone and mud houses abandoned a few decades ago, with the remains of its mosque and minaret above the shore – a quiet, atmospheric place where the old way of life feels close. After lunch (not included) on the way, you cross to the east coast and the mangroves of Al Thakhira, the largest in Qatar. At high tide you can paddle a kayak through the channels (optional, paid locally); at low tide you walk along the shore to watch crabs, herons and, in winter, flamingos.

The last stops are Purple Island – Jazirat Bin Ghanim – a mangrove-fringed island reached by a causeway, named after the purple dye that people of the Kassite period made here from sea snails some 3,500 years ago, and the harbour of Al Khor, Qatar's old pearling port, with its dhows and watchtowers. You arrive back in Doha in the late afternoon.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
08:00 – Pick-up at your hotel in Doha.
09:30 – Al Zubarah Archaeological Site and Al Zubarah Fort (about 1 hour 15 minutes).
11:00 – Al Jumail abandoned village (about 30 minutes).
12:15 – Lunch on the way (not included).
13:30 – Al Thakhira mangroves: kayak or shore walk (about 1 hour).
14:45 – Purple Island (about 30 minutes).
15:30 – Al Khor harbour and corniche (about 20 minutes).
16:30 – Return to your hotel in Doha.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Kayaking depends on the tide; we plan the order of the day around it and confirm when your request is accepted.
• Al Zubarah Fort is free to visit and closed on some days; your guide adapts the schedule.
• About 300 km of good roads in total.

INCLUDED: private vehicle and driver, English-speaking local guide, bottled water, hotel pick-up.
NOT INCLUDED: kayak rental, lunch, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: none.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose your date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only once your tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Where does the tour start and finish?
faq.answer: At your hotel anywhere in Doha. The day lasts about eight hours, and we can adjust the start time to suit you.

faq.question: Is the tour private?
faq.answer: Yes. The car, driver and guide are for you and your group only.

faq.question: Is Al Zubarah really a UNESCO site?
faq.answer: Yes. The Al Zubarah Archaeological Site was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2013, the first site in Qatar. It preserves a walled pearl-trading town of the 18th and 19th centuries.

faq.question: Is the kayak included?
faq.answer: No. Kayaks are rented from local providers at Al Thakhira and paid on the spot, usually for one to two hours. It depends on the tide, so we confirm the timing when we accept your request.

faq.question: Do I need to be fit to kayak?
faq.answer: No. The water in the mangroves is calm and shallow, and double kayaks make it easy for beginners and families. If you prefer, you can simply walk along the shore.

faq.question: What wildlife can we see?
faq.answer: Crabs and small fish in the mangroves, herons, egrets and cormorants, and in winter flamingos and other migrating birds. Bring binoculars if you have them.

faq.question: Are entrance fees included?
faq.answer: Al Zubarah Fort, Al Jumail, Purple Island and Al Khor are free to visit. Only the optional kayak is paid locally.

faq.question: Where do we have lunch?
faq.answer: Usually in a simple local restaurant on the way or in Al Khor, where fresh fish is a speciality. Lunch is not included.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children and older travellers?
faq.answer: Yes. Walks are short and on level ground, and the car is always close by. Child seats are available on request.

faq.question: What should I bring?
faq.answer: A hat, sunglasses, sunscreen, comfortable shoes, and swimwear or a change of clothes if you plan to kayak. Insect repellent is useful near the mangroves.

faq.question: When is the best time of year?
faq.answer: November to April, when the weather is pleasant and migrating birds are in the mangroves. In summer we start very early to avoid the midday heat.

faq.question: What is your cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Before your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
